source: Official immigration and consular sites; reviewed in pull requests

AE.name: Visa on arrival / visa-free entry
AE.purpose: Nationalities eligible for entry without a pre-arranged visa (e.g. Serbia, the EU, the UK, the US).
AE.note: 30 or 90 days depending on nationality — the rule for your passport is shown above.

AE.name: Tourist visa (30 or 60 days)
AE.purpose: Tourism, single or multiple entry, sponsored by a hotel, airline or tour operator.
AE.maxValidity: Single or multiple entry, valid 60 days from issue
AE.note: Stay of 30 or 60 days, extendable once in the UAE.

AE.name: 5-year multiple-entry tourist visa
AE.purpose: Frequent tourists with sufficient funds; self-sponsored.
AE.note: Up to 90 days per stay, extendable once by 90 days; at most 180 days a year.

AE.name: Visit visa (family, friends, job exploration, business)
AE.purpose: Visiting relatives or friends, exploring jobs, business visits, attending events.
AE.note: Stays of 30, 60 or 90 days depending on the kind of visit.

AE.name: Transit visa
AE.purpose: Passing through the UAE on the way to another country.

AE.name: Medical treatment entry permit
AE.purpose: Patients coming for treatment in the UAE, and their companions.

AE.name: Work residence visa
AE.purpose: Employment with a UAE company or government entity sponsoring you.
AE.note: No day count, but leaving for more than 6 months can cancel residence.

AE.name: Student residence visa
AE.purpose: Studying at a UAE university or school; outstanding students can get longer visas.
AE.maxValidity: 1 year, renewable (5 years for outstanding students)

AE.name: Family residence visa
AE.purpose: Spouse, children and parents sponsored by a UAE resident.

AE.name: Retirement residence visa
AE.purpose: Residents aged 55 or over with savings, property or income above the thresholds.

AE.name: Remote work visa
AE.purpose: Working for an employer outside the UAE while living in the UAE.

AE.name: Investor / partner residence visa
AE.purpose: Investors and partners in a UAE company, and property owners.
AE.maxValidity: 2 or 3 years; golden visa for larger investments

AE.name: Golden visa
AE.purpose: Long-term residence for investors, entrepreneurs, specialised talents, outstanding students and others; no sponsor needed.
AE.note: Residence is kept even with long absences abroad.

AE.name: Blue visa
AE.purpose: Long-term residence for people who contribute to protecting the environment and sustainability.

AU.name: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601)
AU.purpose: Tourism or business visitor activities for eligible passport holders, applied for in the Australian ETA app.
AU.note: Up to 3 months after each entry. Study or training up to 3 months in total.

AU.name: eVisitor (subclass 651)
AU.purpose: Tourism or business visitor activities for EU and some other European passport holders. Free.
AU.note: Up to 3 months after each entry.

AU.name: Visitor (subclass 600)
AU.purpose: Tourism, visiting family, business visitor activities or sponsored family visits, for any nationality.
AU.note: Each grant allows a stay of 3, 6 or 12 months — the period on your grant letter is what counts.

AU.name: Transit visa (subclass 771)
AU.purpose: Passing through Australia, or joining a ship as crew.
AU.note: No longer than 72 hours (5 days to sign on to a ship as crew).

AU.name: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602)
AU.purpose: Medical treatment or consultations in Australia, or supporting someone who is.
AU.note: Temporary; the stay is set on your grant.

AU.name: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417)
AU.purpose: Holiday and short-term work for 18–30 year olds (35 for some countries) from partner countries.
AU.maxValidity: 12 months; a 2nd and 3rd year possible with specified work

AU.name: Work and Holiday visa (subclass 462)
AU.purpose: Holiday and short-term work for 18–30 year olds from partner countries (education and English requirements).
AU.maxValidity: 12 months; a 2nd and 3rd year possible with specified work

AU.name: Student visa (subclass 500)
AU.purpose: Full-time study at a registered course.
AU.maxValidity: Up to 6 years, in line with your enrolment

AU.name: Student Guardian visa (subclass 590)
AU.purpose: Guardians of student visa holders under 18.
AU.maxValidity: Linked to the student visa holder

AU.name: Training visa (subclass 407)
AU.purpose: Workplace-based training or professional development.

AU.name: Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482)
AU.purpose: Skilled work for an approved Australian employer that cannot find a local worker.

AU.name: Temporary Work (Short Stay Specialist) visa (subclass 400)
AU.purpose: Short-term, highly specialised, non-ongoing work.
AU.note: Usually up to 3 months; longer needs a strong business case.

AU.name: Temporary Activity visa (subclass 408)
AU.purpose: Short-term work in specific activities: entertainment, sport, research, religious work, events, exchanges.
AU.maxValidity: From 3 months to 4 years, depending on the activity

AU.name: Temporary Work (International Relations) visa (subclass 403)
AU.purpose: Work under government agreements: diplomats' private staff, Pacific Australia Labour Mobility, foreign government agencies.
AU.maxValidity: Up to 4 years, depending on the stream

AU.name: Crew Travel Authority (subclass 942)
AU.purpose: International airline crew.
AU.maxValidity: Until you stop working as airline crew
AU.note: Crew members and safety inspectors up to 30 days at a time.

AU.name: Maritime Crew visa (subclass 988)
AU.purpose: Crew of non-military ships arriving in Australia.
AU.note: You may stay as long as you are crew of an eligible ship that is in Australia.

AU.name: Special Purpose visa
AU.purpose: People with a prescribed status — e.g. military personnel, guests of government, some airline crew.
AU.maxValidity: As long as you have the prescribed status

AU.name: Special Category visa (subclass 444)
AU.purpose: New Zealand citizens living and working in Australia; granted on arrival.
AU.note: No day count while you stay.

AU.name: New Zealand Citizen Family Relationship (temporary) visa (subclass 461)
AU.purpose: Family members of New Zealand citizens living in Australia.

AU.name: Partner visa — outside Australia (subclass 309/100)
AU.purpose: Spouse or de facto partner of an Australian citizen, permanent resident or eligible New Zealander, applying from outside Australia.
AU.maxValidity: Temporary (309) until the permanent visa (100) is decided

AU.name: Partner visa — in Australia (subclass 820/801)
AU.purpose: Spouse or de facto partner of an Australian citizen, permanent resident or eligible New Zealander, applying in Australia.
AU.maxValidity: Temporary (820) until the permanent visa (801) is decided

AU.name: Prospective Marriage visa (subclass 300)
AU.purpose: Coming to Australia to marry your Australian partner, then apply for a partner visa.

AU.name: Parent visa (subclass 103)
AU.purpose: Parents of a settled Australian citizen, permanent resident or eligible New Zealander.

AU.name: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804)
AU.purpose: Parents of pension age of a settled Australian, applying in Australia.

AU.name: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 173/143)
AU.purpose: Parents of a settled Australian, with a higher contribution and faster processing.

AU.name: Contributory Aged Parent visa (subclass 884/864)
AU.purpose: Parents of pension age of a settled Australian, applying in Australia, with a higher contribution.

AU.name: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870)
AU.purpose: Parents visiting their Australian children for longer periods.

AU.name: Child visa (subclass 101/802)
AU.purpose: Dependent children of an Australian citizen, permanent resident or eligible New Zealander.

AU.name: Dependent Child visa (subclass 445)
AU.purpose: Dependent children of a partner visa holder.
AU.maxValidity: Until the parent's permanent visa is decided

AU.name: Adoption visa (subclass 102)
AU.purpose: Children adopted, or being adopted, by Australian citizens or permanent residents.

AU.name: Orphan Relative visa (subclass 117/837)
AU.purpose: Children under 18 whose parents cannot care for them, sponsored by an Australian relative.

AU.name: Remaining Relative visa (subclass 115/835)
AU.purpose: People whose only close family are in Australia.

AU.name: Aged Dependent Relative visa (subclass 114/838)
AU.purpose: Older, single relatives financially dependent on an Australian relative.

AU.name: Carer visa (subclass 116/836)
AU.purpose: Caring for an Australian relative with a long-term medical condition.

AU.name: Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189)
AU.purpose: Invited skilled workers with an occupation on the skilled list, no sponsor needed.

AU.name: Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190)
AU.purpose: Skilled workers nominated by a state or territory.

AU.name: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491)
AU.purpose: Skilled workers living and working in regional Australia, nominated by a state or sponsored by family.

AU.name: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (provisional) visa (subclass 494)
AU.purpose: Skilled workers sponsored by a regional employer.

AU.name: Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) visa (subclass 191)
AU.purpose: Holders of a 491 or 494 visa who lived and worked in regional Australia.

AU.name: Skilled Regional (provisional) visa (subclass 489)
AU.purpose: Older regional skilled visa (closed to new applicants except some family members).

AU.name: Skilled Regional visa (subclass 887)
AU.purpose: Holders of certain provisional regional visas who lived and worked in regional Australia.

AU.name: Employer Nomination Scheme (subclass 186)
AU.purpose: Skilled workers nominated by an Australian employer.

AU.name: Regional Sponsored Migration Scheme (subclass 187)
AU.purpose: Skilled workers nominated by a regional employer (mostly closed to new applicants).

AU.name: Pacific Engagement Visa (subclass 192)
AU.purpose: Citizens of Pacific countries and Timor-Leste selected in the annual ballot.

AU.name: National Innovation visa (subclass 858)
AU.purpose: People with an internationally recognised record of exceptional achievement.

AU.name: Distinguished Talent visa (subclass 124)
AU.purpose: People with an internationally recognised record of exceptional achievement, applying from outside Australia.

AU.name: Business Innovation and Investment (provisional) visa (subclass 188)
AU.purpose: Business owners and investors (closed to new applicants).

AU.name: Business Talent (Permanent) visa (subclass 132)
AU.purpose: High-level business owners and entrepreneurs (closed to new applicants).

AU.name: Refugee visas (subclass 200, 201, 203, 204)
AU.purpose: People outside their home country who are subject to persecution.

AU.name: Global Special Humanitarian (subclass 202)
AU.purpose: People subject to substantial discrimination, proposed by someone in Australia.

AU.name: Protection visa (subclass 866)
AU.purpose: People in Australia who engage Australia's protection obligations.

AU.name: Temporary Protection visa (subclass 785)
AU.purpose: People who arrived without a valid visa and engage Australia's protection obligations.

AU.name: Safe Haven Enterprise visa (subclass 790)
AU.purpose: People who arrived without a valid visa, engage protection obligations and want to work or study in regional Australia.

AU.name: Bridging visa A (subclass 010)
AU.purpose: Staying lawfully in Australia while a new substantive visa application is processed.

AU.name: Bridging visa B (subclass 020)
AU.purpose: Travelling out of and back into Australia while a substantive visa application is processed.
AU.maxValidity: Temporary; the travel period is set on the grant

AU.name: Bridging visa C (subclass 030)
AU.purpose: Staying lawfully while an application is processed, when you had no substantive visa.

AU.name: Bridging visa E (subclass 050/051)
AU.purpose: Staying lawfully while you arrange to leave, or while a matter is resolved.

AU.name: Resident Return visa (subclass 155/157)
AU.purpose: Permanent residents and former citizens travelling back to Australia as permanent residents.
AU.note: No day count in Australia; it only governs re-entry.

AU.name: Former Resident visa (subclass 151)
AU.purpose: Former residents who spent their childhood in Australia or served in the Australian Defence Force.

CA.name: Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA)
CA.purpose: Flying to or through Canada as a visitor, for visa-exempt nationalities.
CA.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (or until the passport expires)
CA.note: Not a visa. The border officer decides how long you may stay, usually up to 6 months.

CA.name: Visitor visa (temporary resident visa)
CA.purpose: Tourism, visiting family or friends, for nationalities that need a visa.
CA.maxValidity: Up to 10 years or until the passport expires
CA.note: The border officer decides how long you may stay, usually up to 6 months; the date may be stamped in your passport or on a visitor record.

CA.name: Business visitor
CA.purpose: Business meetings, conferences, trade shows and events, without entering the Canadian labour market.
CA.maxValidity: Uses your eTA or visitor visa

CA.name: Parent and grandparent super visa
CA.purpose: Parents and grandparents visiting children or grandchildren who are Canadian citizens or permanent residents.
CA.note: Up to 5 years at a time per entry.

CA.name: Transit visa
CA.purpose: Travelling through a Canadian airport to another country within 48 hours, for nationalities that need a visa.

CA.name: Visitor record (extend your stay)
CA.purpose: Staying longer in Canada as a visitor than the date you were given.

CA.name: Study permit
CA.purpose: Studying at a designated learning institution for longer than 6 months.
CA.maxValidity: Length of the program plus 90 days
CA.note: Allows some work while you study, with conditions.

CA.name: Post-graduation work permit
CA.purpose: Working in Canada after graduating from an eligible Canadian program.
CA.maxValidity: Up to 3 years, depending on the program

CA.name: Employer-specific work permit
CA.purpose: Working for one employer under the conditions on your permit (often needs an LMIA).
CA.maxValidity: As on the permit (usually the length of the job offer)

CA.name: Open work permit
CA.purpose: Working for almost any employer — e.g. spouses of skilled workers or students, people waiting for permanent residence.

CA.name: International Experience Canada (working holiday, young professionals, co-op)
CA.purpose: Young people (usually 18–35) from partner countries travelling and working in Canada.
CA.maxValidity: Usually 12 to 24 months, depending on your country

CA.name: Work permit while waiting for permanent residence
CA.purpose: Working while your permanent residence application is processed (bridging open work permit).

CA.name: Open work permit for family of foreign workers
CA.purpose: Spouses, common-law partners and dependent children of foreign workers in Canada.

CA.name: Express Entry (permanent residence)
CA.purpose: Skilled workers: Federal Skilled Worker, Canadian Experience Class and Federal Skilled Trades.

CA.name: Provincial Nominee Program
CA.purpose: Permanent residence nominated by a province or territory for its labour needs.

CA.name: Atlantic Immigration Program
CA.purpose: Permanent residence with a job offer in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, PEI or Newfoundland and Labrador.

CA.name: Rural and Francophone Community Immigration Pilots
CA.purpose: Permanent residence with a job in a participating rural or francophone community.

CA.name: Quebec-selected skilled workers, investors and entrepreneurs
CA.purpose: Permanent residence through selection by Quebec.

CA.name: Caregivers (permanent residence)
CA.purpose: Home child-care and home support workers.

CA.name: Medical doctors (permanent residence)
CA.purpose: Physicians with Canadian work experience.

CA.name: Family sponsorship
CA.purpose: Spouses, partners, dependent children, parents and grandparents sponsored by a Canadian citizen or permanent resident.

CA.name: Start-up Visa / Self-employed persons
CA.purpose: Entrepreneurs with an innovative business, or self-employed people in culture or athletics.
CA.note: Both programs were paused when last checked.

CA.name: Permanent resident card
CA.purpose: Proof of permanent resident status for travelling back to Canada.
CA.note: No day count, but you must live in Canada at least 730 days in every 5 years to keep the status.

CY.name: Visa-free short stay
CY.purpose: Short stays for nationalities that do not need a Cyprus visa (e.g. Serbia, the US, the UK).
CY.note: Up to 90 days in any 180-day period in Cyprus. Valid only for the Republic of Cyprus until Cyprus fully joins Schengen; days in Cyprus do not count towards the Schengen 90/180.

CY.name: Short-stay visa (type C, 1 or 2 entries)
CY.purpose: Tourism, business or family visits of up to 90 days.
CY.note: Valid only for the Republic of Cyprus until Cyprus fully joins Schengen; days in Cyprus do not count towards the Schengen 90/180.

CY.name: Multiple-entry short-stay visa (type C – MEV)
CY.purpose: Frequent travellers to Cyprus with a good visa history.
CY.note: Never more than 90 days in any 180-day period. Valid only for the Republic of Cyprus until Cyprus fully joins Schengen; days in Cyprus do not count towards the Schengen 90/180.

CY.name: Border visa for transit or short stay (type C – LTV)
CY.purpose: Issued at the border only in emergencies, with the approval of the Migration Department.

CY.name: Airport transit visa (type A – ATV)
CY.purpose: Staying in the international transit zone of a Cypriot airport — for the nationalities that need it.
CY.note: Does not allow entry into Cyprus.

GB.name: Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
GB.purpose: Visit for tourism, family, business or short study without a visa — for nationalities that do not need a visa.
GB.note: Not a visa. Up to 6 months per visit.

GB.name: Standard Visitor visa
GB.purpose: Tourism, visiting family, business meetings, short courses up to 6 months, medical treatment, academic visits.
GB.note: At most 6 months on each visit, even with a long-term visa. You must not live in the UK through frequent visits.

GB.name: Marriage Visitor visa
GB.purpose: Getting married or registering a civil partnership in the UK (not living there afterwards).

GB.name: Permitted Paid Engagement visa
GB.purpose: Paid work for up to 1 month by invitation: lectures, examining, performing, sports events, professional services.

GB.name: Visitor in Transit visa
GB.purpose: Passing through UK border control and leaving the UK within 48 hours.
GB.note: You must leave within 48 hours. Staying longer needs a Standard Visitor visa.

GB.name: Direct Airside Transit visa
GB.purpose: Changing flights without going through UK border control — for nationalities that need it.
GB.note: Does not allow entry into the UK.

GB.name: Student visa
GB.purpose: Study a course at a licensed university, college or school (age 16 or over).
GB.maxValidity: Length of the course plus a few months

GB.name: Child Student visa
GB.purpose: Children aged 4–17 studying at an independent school in the UK.
GB.maxValidity: Length of the course plus a few months

GB.name: Short-term study visa (English language)
GB.purpose: English language courses of 6 to 11 months.

GB.name: Graduate visa
GB.purpose: Stay and work after successfully finishing a UK degree.
GB.maxValidity: 2 years (18 months if you apply from 1 January 2027); 3 years after a PhD

GB.name: Skilled Worker visa
GB.purpose: A job with an approved UK employer (sponsor) at the required skill and salary level; family can join.
GB.maxValidity: Up to 5 years, then extend or settle

GB.name: Health and Care Worker visa
GB.purpose: Doctors, nurses, health and adult social care professionals working for the NHS or approved employers.

GB.name: Global Talent visa
GB.purpose: Leaders or potential leaders in academia, research, arts and culture or digital technology.
GB.maxValidity: Up to 5 years at a time

GB.name: High Potential Individual visa
GB.purpose: Recent graduates of top world universities, no job offer needed.

GB.name: Scale-up Worker visa
GB.purpose: A highly skilled job with a fast-growing UK business.

GB.name: Innovator Founder visa
GB.purpose: Setting up an innovative, endorsed business in the UK.

GB.name: Youth Mobility Scheme visa
GB.purpose: Live and work for up to 2 years — aged 18–30 (35 for some countries) from participating countries.

GB.name: Seasonal Worker visa
GB.purpose: Seasonal horticulture or poultry work.
GB.maxValidity: Up to 6 months (horticulture) or 2 Oct–31 Dec (poultry)
GB.note: At most 6 months in any 12-month period.

GB.name: Creative Worker visa
GB.purpose: Short-term work in the creative industry: actors, musicians, dancers, film crew.

GB.name: Charity Worker visa
GB.purpose: Unpaid voluntary work for a licensed charity.

GB.name: Religious Worker visa
GB.purpose: Temporary religious work, such as preaching or working in a religious order.

GB.name: Minister of Religion visa
GB.purpose: A job as a minister, missionary or member of a religious order.

GB.name: Government Authorised Exchange visa
GB.purpose: Work experience, training, research or fellowships through an approved exchange scheme.
GB.maxValidity: Up to 12 or 24 months depending on the scheme

GB.name: International Agreement visa
GB.purpose: Work covered by international law: private servants of diplomats, employees of overseas governments or international organisations.

GB.name: Sportsperson visa
GB.purpose: Elite sportspeople and qualified coaches.
GB.maxValidity: Up to 3 years (longer as a sponsored sportsperson)

GB.name: Global Business Mobility visas
GB.purpose: Moving to a UK branch of your employer: Senior or Specialist Worker, Graduate Trainee, UK Expansion Worker, Service Supplier, Secondment Worker.
GB.maxValidity: Up to 1–5 years depending on the route

GB.name: Overseas Domestic Worker visa
GB.purpose: Domestic workers coming with their employer to a private household in the UK.

GB.name: Frontier Worker permit
GB.purpose: EU, EEA or Swiss citizens living outside the UK who have worked in the UK since before 2021.

GB.name: Family visa
GB.purpose: Living with a partner, parent or child who is British, settled in the UK or has refugee status.
GB.maxValidity: 2 years 9 months, extendable, leads to settlement

GB.name: UK Ancestry visa
GB.purpose: Commonwealth citizens with a grandparent born in the UK who want to work there.

GB.name: British National (Overseas) visa
GB.purpose: British Nationals (Overseas) from Hong Kong and their family.

GB.name: Indefinite leave to remain (settlement)
GB.purpose: Living in the UK permanently after a qualifying period on another visa.
GB.note: No day count. Absences of more than 2 years can end your settled status.

IE.name: Visa-free visit
IE.purpose: Tourism, visiting family or business meetings for nationalities that do not need an Irish visa (e.g. Serbia, the US, the EU).
IE.note: Up to 90 days, as stamped by the immigration officer at the border. Ireland is not in the Schengen area — days here do not count towards the 90/180 rule.

IE.name: Short Stay 'C' visa
IE.purpose: Visits of less than 90 days: tourism, family, business, short courses, conferences.
IE.maxValidity: Single or multiple entry, up to 5 years for frequent travellers
IE.note: The border officer decides how long you may stay, at most 90 days.

IE.name: British Irish Visa Scheme
IE.purpose: One UK visa that also lets nationals of India and China travel to Ireland.

IE.name: Transit visa
IE.purpose: Changing flights at an Irish airport — for the nationalities that need it.
IE.note: Does not allow you to leave the airport.

IE.name: Long Stay 'D' visa
IE.purpose: Coming for more than 90 days to study, work or join family; you then register for a residence permission (Stamp).
IE.maxValidity: Single entry; residence is then set by your Stamp

IE.name: Critical Skills Employment Permit
IE.purpose: Highly skilled jobs on the Critical Skills Occupations List, or other jobs above a high salary threshold.

IE.name: General Employment Permit
IE.purpose: Jobs not on the Ineligible Occupations List, with a labour market needs test.
IE.maxValidity: Up to 2 years, renewable up to 3 more

IE.name: Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permit
IE.purpose: Senior managers, key staff and trainees moving to the Irish branch of their employer.

IE.name: Dependant / Partner / Spouse Employment Permit
IE.purpose: Spouses, partners and dependants of Critical Skills permit holders and some researchers.

IE.name: Reactivation Employment Permit
IE.purpose: People who fell out of the employment permit system through no fault of their own.

IE.name: Contract for Services Employment Permit
IE.purpose: Employees of foreign companies working on a contract for an Irish company.

IE.name: Internship Employment Permit
IE.purpose: Full-time students at a third-level institution outside Ireland doing work experience.

IE.name: Sport and Cultural Employment Permit
IE.purpose: Work in sport or culture that adds to the quality of Irish sport and cultural life.

IE.name: Exchange Agreement Employment Permit
IE.purpose: Work under international exchange agreements, such as the Fulbright programme or AIESEC.

IE.name: Working Holiday Authorisation
IE.purpose: Young people (usually 18–30) from partner countries holidaying and working in Ireland.
IE.maxValidity: Usually 12 months (2 years for some countries)

IE.name: Student permission (Stamp 2 / 2A)
IE.purpose: Full-time study on an approved course (Stamp 2); Stamp 2A for courses not on the list, no work.
IE.maxValidity: Length of the course, with study time limits
IE.note: Stamp 2 allows up to 20 hours of work a week in term time.

IE.name: Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G)
IE.purpose: Graduates of Irish third-level degrees looking for work.
IE.maxValidity: 12 months (24 months after a master's or higher)

IE.name: Stamp 0 — temporary stay without work
IE.purpose: Retiring to Ireland, dependent adult relatives, visiting academics.
IE.note: No work allowed. Not reckonable for citizenship.

IE.name: Stamp 1 — work or business permission
IE.purpose: Living in Ireland on an employment permit, business permission or working holiday.

IE.name: Stamp 3 — family of a permit holder
IE.purpose: Spouses, partners and children of employment permit holders and some researchers or religious ministers.

IE.name: Stamp 4 — long-term residence
IE.purpose: Living and working freely, e.g. after 2 years on a Critical Skills permit, spouses of Irish citizens, long-term residents.

IE.name: Stamp 5 — without condition as to time
IE.purpose: Residence without time limit after at least 8 years of lawful residence.
IE.maxValidity: Without time limit (until the passport expires)

IE.name: Investor and entrepreneur routes
IE.purpose: Starting an innovative business (Start-up Entrepreneur Programme) or investing in Ireland.
IE.note: The Immigrant Investor Programme closed to new applications in 2023.

JP.name: Visa exemption (short-term stay)
JP.purpose: Tourism, business meetings or visiting relatives without a visa — for visa-exempt nationalities.
JP.note: Usually up to 90 days per stay (15 or 30 days for some nationalities). No paid work.

JP.name: Temporary Visitor visa (short-term stay)
JP.purpose: Tourism, business meetings, conferences or visiting relatives, for nationalities that need a visa.
JP.maxValidity: Single entry 3 months; multiple-entry up to 5 years for some nationalities
JP.note: The period of stay (15, 30 or 90 days) is set when you land and stamped in your passport.

JP.name: JAPAN eVISA (short-term stay)
JP.purpose: Online single-entry short-term visa for residents of eligible countries.
JP.maxValidity: 3 months, single entry

JP.name: Visa for Medical Stay
JP.purpose: Medical treatment in Japan, and accompanying persons.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 3 years (multiple entry)
JP.note: Each stay up to 90 days, or 6 months to 1 year when hospitalisation is needed.

JP.name: Working Holiday
JP.purpose: Holiday with short-term work for young people (usually 18–30) from partner countries.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 1 year

JP.name: Highly Skilled Professional (incl. J-Skip)
JP.purpose: Highly skilled researchers, engineers and business managers scoring enough points, or meeting J-Skip income/education thresholds.
JP.maxValidity: 5 years (type i); unlimited (type ii)

JP.name: Professor
JP.purpose: Research or teaching at a Japanese university.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Artist
JP.purpose: Artistic activities that bring income (composers, painters, writers…).
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Religious activities
JP.purpose: Missionary or religious work sent by a foreign religious organisation.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Journalist
JP.purpose: Reporting for a foreign news organisation.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Business manager
JP.purpose: Starting, running or managing a business in Japan.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Legal / Accounting services
JP.purpose: Lawyers, accountants and other licensed legal or accounting professionals.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Medical services
JP.purpose: Doctors, dentists, nurses and other licensed medical professionals.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Researcher
JP.purpose: Research under a contract with a public or private organisation in Japan.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Instructor
JP.purpose: Language or other teaching at elementary, junior high or high schools.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Engineer / Specialist in Humanities / International Services
JP.purpose: Engineers, IT, interpreters, designers, marketing and other office professionals.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Nursing care
JP.purpose: Certified care workers working in nursing care.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Intra-company transferee
JP.purpose: Transfer to a Japanese office of your employer.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Entertainer
JP.purpose: Performing in theatre, music, sports or entertainment.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 3 years

JP.name: Skilled labor
JP.purpose: Work needing special skills: chefs of foreign cuisine, sports trainers, pilots, sommeliers…
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (granted as 3 months, 1, 3 or 5 years), renewable

JP.name: Specified Skilled Worker (i) / (ii)
JP.purpose: Work in sectors with labour shortages (care, construction, food service, manufacturing, agriculture…) after skills and Japanese tests.
JP.maxValidity: (i) up to 5 years in total; (ii) renewable without limit, family can join

JP.name: Technical intern training
JP.purpose: On-the-job technical intern training programmes (being replaced by Employment for Skill Development).
JP.maxValidity: Up to 1–2 years per stage, at most 5 years

JP.name: Cultural activities
JP.purpose: Unpaid study of Japanese culture or arts, such as tea ceremony or martial arts.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 3 years

JP.name: Student
JP.purpose: Study at a university, college, high school or Japanese language school.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 4 years 3 months

JP.name: Training
JP.purpose: Learning skills at a public or private organisation (not technical intern training).
JP.maxValidity: Up to 1 year

JP.name: Dependent (family stay)
JP.purpose: Spouse or children of a foreign resident working or studying in Japan.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years

JP.name: Spouse or child of Japanese national
JP.purpose: Spouse, or biological or specially adopted child, of a Japanese national.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years

JP.name: Spouse or child of permanent resident
JP.purpose: Spouse or child born in Japan of a permanent resident.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years

JP.name: Long-term resident
JP.purpose: People of Japanese descent and others granted residence for special reasons.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years or as designated

JP.name: Designated activities (incl. digital nomads)
JP.purpose: Activities designated individually: e.g. digital nomads (up to 6 months), job-seeking graduates, interns, domestic workers of diplomats.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years or as designated
JP.note: The digital-nomad stay is limited to 6 months.

JP.name: Diplomat
JP.purpose: Diplomatic missions and their families.
JP.maxValidity: For the duration of the mission

JP.name: Official
JP.purpose: Officials of foreign governments or international organisations on official duty.
JP.maxValidity: Up to 5 years

JP.name: Permanent resident
JP.purpose: Living in Japan permanently, usually after 10 years of residence (shorter for highly skilled professionals and spouses).
JP.maxValidity: Permanent
JP.note: No day count. Leave with a re-entry permit, or the status can lapse.

NZ.name: Academic Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are an academic with research or academic work experience, and visiting New Zealand to take part in teaching, education, professional management or research.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Arts and Music Festival Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are a performer or support crew you can apply to visit New Zealand to take part in an arts or music festival. You must be invited by an approved arts or music festival.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Escort of Medical Patients Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa to escort a patient coming to New Zealand for medical treatment or consultation. You must be needed because of the patient's condition.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 6 months on this visa.

NZ.name: German Law Student Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are a German law student or law graduate and you want to visit New Zealand as an unpaid observer in a New Zealand law firm.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 6 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Group Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are applying as a group who will be arriving in and visiting New Zealand together for the same purpose. One person must submit and pay for the group application with a completed Visitor Visa application for each group member.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 1 month on this visa.

NZ.name: Medical Treatment Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa to visit New Zealand for medical treatment or consultation. You must be able to pay for your treatment, unless it is funded under a special arrangement.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 6 months on this visa.

NZ.name: New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority (NZeTA)
NZ.purpose: Some people can use an NZeTA to travel to New Zealand without applying for a visa first. This depends on your passport, how you are travelling and if you are visiting or only transiting.
NZ.note: Not a visa. Visits of up to 3 months (6 months for UK citizens), at most 6 months in any 12-month period.

NZ.name: Occupational Registration Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you want to come to New Zealand to get your New Zealand occupational registration. You can also apply if you are already in New Zealand, have applied for residence, and need more time to obtain your occupational registration.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Pitcairn Islander Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are a Pitcairn Islander, you can visit New Zealand on this visa. You will need enough money to support yourself while you are here and for your return travel.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 6 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Private Yacht or Plane Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: You can travel in and out of New Zealand on a private plane or yacht for up to 6 months on this visa.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Short-term Entertainment Act Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are a performer or support crew member travelling to New Zealand for a live entertainment act. The act must be promoted by an approved promoter.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Sports Events Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa lets you visit New Zealand for a sports event or tour if you are a sports person, a support staff member, a match or tournament official, or a media or broadcasting worker.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Super Yachts Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa is for owners and crew of super yachts travelling to New Zealand. It allows you to stay or travel in and out of New Zealand for up to 6 months.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 6 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Temporary Retirement Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are aged 66 or older and have NZD $750,000 to invest in New Zealand, this visa lets you stay in New Zealand for up to 2 years.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 2 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Tour Escort Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: You can come to New Zealand as a tour escort with this visa. You must have a letter from your employer confirming your role as a tour escort before you apply.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 9 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Visa Waiver Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are eligible for a New Zealand Travel Authority (NZeTA) you may be able to travel to New Zealand without a visa. If given entry permission, we give you a Visa Waiver Visitor Visa when you arrive.
NZ.note: Given on arrival to NZeTA holders: up to 3 months (6 months for UK citizens).

NZ.name: Visiting Media Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are taking part in Tourism New Zealand's Visiting Media Programme.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 1 month on this visa.

NZ.name: Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: People travelling on a passport from some countries must apply for a Visitor Visa to visit New Zealand. You can stay for up to either 6 months or 9 months. You cannot work, but you can study for up to 3 months.
NZ.note: Up to 6 or 9 months per visit, and at most 9 months in any 18-month period.

NZ.name: APEC Business Travel Card to visit New Zealand
NZ.purpose: If you have an APEC Business Travel Card (ABTC), you can visit New Zealand for up to 3 months at a time to carry out trade and investment activities. New Zealand needs to be listed on your card as an economy that has pre-cleared you for short-term business travel here.

NZ.name: Active Investor Plus Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa to live, work and invest in New Zealand. You must have at least NZD $5 million to apply under the Growth category or at least NZD $10 million to apply under the Balanced category.

NZ.name: Business Investor Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you want to invest in and operate a business in New Zealand. You must invest at least NZD $1 million in an established business.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 4 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Business Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you want to visit New Zealand for business reasons. You must have enough money to live on while you are here or have the financial support of your employer.
NZ.note: Up to 3 months in 1 year.

NZ.name: Entrepreneur Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you want to work in your own business in New Zealand. You must have NZD $100,000 to invest, a business plan, and be able to claim 120 points on our points scale.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Antarctic Traveller Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply to transit through New Zealand to work in Antarctica for a Contracting Party as part of a scientific programme or expedition under the Antarctic Treaty.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 1 year on this visa.

NZ.name: Transit Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are passing through Auckland International Airport you must have a Transit Visa unless you already have a valid visa, are from a visa waiver country or transit visa waiver country, or are travelling to or from Australia.
NZ.note: You must stay in the transit area of Auckland Airport, at most 24 hours.

NZ.name: Dependent Child Student Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa to bring your dependent children to study at primary or secondary school in New Zealand. You must have an appropriate work or student visa.

NZ.name: English Language Student Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa to study an English language course full-time in New Zealand. You will need to pay the full cost of your courses and enrol with an approved education provider.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 4 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Exchange Student Visa
NZ.purpose: If you have been accepted into an approved student exchange scheme and are outside New Zealand, you can apply for this visa to study full-time in New Zealand.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 4 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Fee Paying Student Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa is for students who are paying international tuition fees themselves, or with support from family, a loan, or a partial scholarship. You must have an offer of place from an approved education provider.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 4 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Foreign Government Supported Student Visa
NZ.purpose: If you have a foreign government scholarship, you can apply for this visa to study full-time in New Zealand for more than 3 months.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 4 years on this visa.

NZ.name: NZ Government Scholarship Student Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are funded by a New Zealand scholarship administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) or Education New Zealand (ENZ), you can apply to study full-time on this visa.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 4 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Partner of a Student Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa to work in New Zealand if your partner is studying for an eligible level 7 or 8 qualification, or a level 9 or 10 qualification on the New Zealand Qualifications and Credentials Framework (NZQCF).

NZ.name: Partner of an NZ Scholarship Student Work Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa allows you to work in New Zealand while your partner is here on an MFAT-funded NZ Scholarship.

NZ.name: Pathway Student Visa
NZ.purpose: You can study up to 3 courses, 1 after the other, on this visa. You must have a Pathway Student Visa offer of place and the funds to pay for your tuition fees and living costs.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 5 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Student and Trainee Work Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa is for students or trainees wanting to get practical work experience in their field. This can include, but is not limited to, religious trainees, dental or medical trainees and apprentice jockeys.

NZ.name: Trafficking Child Victim Student Visa
NZ.purpose: A child may be given this visa if they are 17 or younger, in New Zealand, and certified by the New Zealand Police as a suspected victim of people trafficking. This visa allows the child to study as a domestic student at primary or secondary school.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 1 year on this visa.

NZ.name: Vocational Trainee Student Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are a trainee who has been awarded a New Zealand Short Term Training Scholarship by Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships, or you are a nautical student.

NZ.name: Accredited Employer Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you have a job offer from an Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV) accredited employer. The employer must send you a link to the online application form.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 5 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Child of a Worker Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: If you have a work visa, you can apply for this visa so your dependent children can visit you in New Zealand and study for up to 3 months.

NZ.name: China Skilled Workers Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you have a job offer for a role on the China skilled job list. You must be a citizen of the People's Republic of China and meet the listed requirements.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: China Special Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you have a job offer as a qualified chef, traditional medicine practitioner, Mandarin teacher's aide, Wushu martial arts coach, or Chinese tourism specialist. You must be a citizen of the People's Republic of China.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Crew joining a Ship or Plane Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are a crew member travelling to New Zealand to join a ship or plane leaving for another country, and you do not have a Crew ETA.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 28 days on this visa.

NZ.name: Dismissed Worker Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: If you have a current work visa and you were dismissed from your job during a trial period, this visa lets you stay in New Zealand for up to 3 months. You cannot work on this visa.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Domestic Staff of a Diplomat Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are a domestic worker for diplomatic, consular or official staff posted in New Zealand. Your employer and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade must support your application.

NZ.name: Entertainers Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you want to work on a film, video or production in New Zealand and you have specific skills that cannot be met by New Zealand's entertainment industry.

NZ.name: Fishing Crew Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa to work as crew on a fishing vessel in New Zealand waters.

NZ.name: Global Workforce Seasonal Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you work in a job on the Global Workforce Seasonal Visa job list. You must be asked to apply by an Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV) accredited employer.

NZ.name: Indonesia Special Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are a citizen of Indonesia and you have a job offer as a trained chef, Halal slaughterer or Bahasa teacher's aide.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Japanese Interpreters Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you have a full-time job offer to work as a qualified interpreter in a tourism-related industry in New Zealand. You must be from Japan.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Long Term Skill Shortage List Work Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa is now closed. You can only apply for this visa if you have already held a Long Term Skill Shortage List Work Visa and you are waiting for a decision on your resident visa application.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 30 months on this visa. Closed to new applicants.

NZ.name: Migrant Exploitation Protection Work Visa
NZ.purpose: If you have reported exploitation while on an employer-supported work visa, this visa will allow you to leave your job while the exploitation is being investigated.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 6 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Partner of Military Work Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa allows you to work in New Zealand while your partner is here on a military visa.

NZ.name: Partner of a New Zealander Work Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa allows you to work in New Zealand if you have a partner who is a New Zealand citizen or has a resident visa.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Partner of a Worker Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa allows you to join your partner while they are in New Zealand on a work visa.

NZ.name: Partner of a Worker Work Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa allows you to work in New Zealand while your partner is here on a work visa. Your partner must have an eligible work visa to support your application.

NZ.name: Peak Seasonal Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you work in a job on the Peak Seasonal Visa job list. Your employer must send you a link to the online application form.

NZ.name: Philippines Special Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are a registered nurse, farm manager or engineering professional from the Philippines. You must have a job offer, qualifications and experience.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Post-Study Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you want to work in New Zealand soon after you have completed your studies here. It allows you to stay and work in New Zealand for up to 3 years, depending on what you studied.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Primary Sector Trainees Work Visa
NZ.purpose: People from Chile and South Korea can do vocational study and take up work placements in primary sector industries in New Zealand. To apply, you must be supported or funded by your government and intend to return home after your training to share your new skills.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 1 year on this visa.

NZ.name: Recognised Seasonal Employer Limited Visa
NZ.purpose: On the Recognised Seasonal Employer Limited Visa you can come to New Zealand for a short time to work in our horticulture and viticulture industries. You must have a job offer from a Recognised Seasonal Employer before you apply.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 7 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Religious Worker Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you have an offer of religious work from a religious organisation.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 2 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Republic of Korea Special Work Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you are a citizen of the Republic of Korea and qualified to work in a Republic of Korea Special Work occupation.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Short-Term Graduate Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you want to work in New Zealand soon after completing your studies here and you are not eligible for a Post-Study Work Visa. It lets you stay and work in New Zealand for up to 6 months while you look for a job and explore longer-term work options.

NZ.name: Singapore Work Exchange Programme Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you want to holiday, study and work in New Zealand. You must be aged 18 to 30 and a citizen of Singapore.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 1 year on this visa.

NZ.name: South Island Contribution Work Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you have an Essential Skills Work Visa and have been employed in the South Island for over 5 years. This visa provides a path to residence if you remain in the same industry and region.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 30 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Specific Purpose Work Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa allows you work in New Zealand for a specific purpose or event.

NZ.name: Supplementary Seasonal Employment Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are already in New Zealand on a student or visitor visa and you want to do seasonal work in the horticulture or viticulture industry.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 6 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Talent (Accredited Employer) Work Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this resident visa if you have been on a Talent (Accredited Employer) Work Visa and have worked for an accredited employer for more than 2 years.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 30 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Talent (Arts, Culture, Sports) Work Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you have an exceptional talent in a field of art, sport or culture.

NZ.name: Thai Chefs Work Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you are a citizen of Thailand, have an offer of full-time work as a Thai chef, and the necessary qualifications and experience to do that work.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Trafficking Victim Work Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you are in New Zealand and certified by the New Zealand Police as a suspected victim of people trafficking.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 1 year on this visa.

NZ.name: Victims of Family Violence Work Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you have experienced family violence and have been in a partnership with a New Zealand citizen or resident, or hold a partnership-based visa with a temporary migrant.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 6 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Vietnam Special Work Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you are a citizen of Vietnam and have been offered work in New Zealand as a chef or engineering professional. You must be qualified to do the job you have been offered.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Work Exchange Scheme Work Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa to work in New Zealand as part of an approved work exchange scheme.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 1 year on this visa.

NZ.name: Working Holiday visas
NZ.purpose: Holiday and work for young people (usually 18–30, 35 for some) from 44 partner countries: Argentina, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Croatia, Czech, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Hong Kong SAR, Hungary, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Korea, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malaysia, Malta, Mexico, Netherlands, Norway, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey, USA, United Kingdom, Uruguay, Vietnam.
NZ.maxValidity: Usually 12 months (23 months for the UK, Canada and some others)
NZ.note: Each partner country has its own working holiday visa with its own rules; check the one for your passport.

NZ.name: Adoption Pre-citizenship Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Children adopted from other countries can visit before their New Zealand citizenship is confirmed. You must provide their birth certificate and evidence that an adoptive parent is a New Zealand citizen.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 6 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Adoption Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Children can come to New Zealand to be adopted by New Zealand citizens or residents. The adoption must have the support of Oranga Tamariki — Ministry for Children.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 6 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Child of Military Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Your dependent children can join you while you are in New Zealand for military work. They can study for up to 3 months and travel in New Zealand while you are here.

NZ.name: Child of a New Zealander Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa allows your dependent children to visit you in New Zealand for up to 9 months. You must be a New Zealand citizen or resident.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 9 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Child of a Student Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: Your dependent children can visit you while you study in New Zealand. They can study for up 3 months. Dependent children must be aged 19 or younger.

NZ.name: Culturally Arranged Marriage Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: If you have recently married a New Zealand citizen or resident in a traditional arranged marriage, or want to marry in New Zealand, you can get a 3-month visitor visa to begin living with your partner.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Guardian Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are a parent or legal guardian of a child who has a current New Zealand student visa, you can apply for this visa to live with and care for your child.

NZ.name: Parent Boost Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you have children who are New Zealand citizens or residents. It allows you to travel in and out of New Zealand to visit your family.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 5 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Parent and Grandparent Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you have children or grandchildren who are New Zealand citizens or residents. It allows you to travel in and out of New Zealand to visit your family.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 6 months on this visa.

NZ.name: Partner of Military Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa allows you to join your partner in New Zealand if they are here on a military visa.

NZ.name: Partner of a New Zealander Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa allows you to visit New Zealand if you have a partner who is a New Zealand citizen or resident.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 3 years on this visa.

NZ.name: Partner of a Student Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa allows you to visit New Zealand if you have a partner who is studying here.

NZ.name: Trafficking Child Victim Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: A child may be given this visa if they are 17 or younger, in New Zealand, and certified by the New Zealand Police as a suspected victim of people trafficking.
NZ.note: Stay of up to 1 year on this visa.

NZ.name: Australian Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are an Australian citizen or permanent resident you can visit, work and live in New Zealand. You can only apply for this visa when you arrive in New Zealand. If you are an Australian permanent resident, you will need an NZeTA.

NZ.name: Business Investor Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you hold a Business Investor Work Visa and have been actively running a business in New Zealand for at least 12 months or 3 years, depending on how much you have invested.

NZ.name: Care Workforce Work to Residence Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this resident visa if you currently have a job or job offer from an accredited employer and have worked in New Zealand for 24 months in a selected care workforce job.

NZ.name: Community Sponsored Refugee Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa is for refugees who have been nominated or matched with an approved community organisation (sponsor) under the Community Organisation Refugee Sponsorship (CORS) Programme.

NZ.name: Dependent Child Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa to bring your dependent children to live with you in New Zealand. You must be a New Zealand citizen or resident.

NZ.name: Employees of Relocating Business Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you are a key employee of a business relocating to New Zealand and you are not eligible for any other resident visa.

NZ.name: Entrepreneur Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you have been self-employed in New Zealand at least 6 months, or have operated a self-employed business for 2 years on another visa.

NZ.name: Global Impact Permanent Residence Visa
NZ.purpose: If you have had a Global Impact Work Visa for 30 months or more, you can apply for this residence visa to live in New Zealand permanently.

NZ.name: Intercountry Adoption Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are a New Zealand citizen or resident, you can apply for this visa to bring an adopted child to live with you in New Zealand indefinitely.

NZ.name: Long Term Skill Shortage List Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: If you have a Long Term Skill Shortage List Work Visa and have worked in New Zealand for more than 2 years, you may be able to apply for this resident visa.

NZ.name: Pacific Access Category Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are from Fiji, Kiribati, Tonga or Tuvalu you can register for this ballot to come to New Zealand. If we select and accept your registration, we invite you to apply for the Pacific Access Category Resident Visa.

NZ.name: Parent Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa allows for a parent, grandparent or legal guardian of a New Zealand citizen or resident to live in New Zealand.

NZ.name: Parent Retirement Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you want to live in New Zealand permanently and you have an adult child who is a New Zealand citizen or resident. You must meet our income and investment requirements.

NZ.name: Partner of a New Zealander Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: You can live in New Zealand on this visa if you have a partner who is a New Zealand citizen or resident.

NZ.name: Permanent Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you have had a resident visa for more than 2 years. This visa lets you live in New Zealand permanently, and travel in and out of the country.

NZ.name: Pitcairn Islander Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are a Pitcairn Islander who has been offered skilled employment in New Zealand, you can apply for this resident visa.

NZ.name: Refugee Family Support Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: To apply for this visa, you must be sponsored by a family member who came to New Zealand as a refugee or protected person.

NZ.name: Religious Worker Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for residence if you have had a Religious Worker Work Visa for 3 years. You must have an offer of ongoing work and sponsorship from your religious organisation.

NZ.name: Samoan Quota Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are a Samoan citizen, you can register for this ballot to come to New Zealand. If we select and accept your registration, we invite you to apply for the Samoan Quota Resident Visa.

NZ.name: Second or Subsequent Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you had a New Zealand resident visa that has expired. Your eligibility will depend on the length of time since your visa expired and your commitment to New Zealand before that.

NZ.name: Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: You can submit an expression of interest (EOI) if you have a job or job offer from an accredited employer, and meet the requirements for one of the Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) pathways.

NZ.name: South Island Contribution Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for New Zealand residence if you have a South Island Contribution Work Visa, and have been employed in the same industry and region for the last 2 years.

NZ.name: Straight to Residence Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you have a job or job offer with an accredited employer, and your job is on Tier 1 of the Green List of in-demand jobs.

NZ.name: Talent (Accredited Employer) Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this resident visa if you have been on a Talent (Accredited Employer) Work Visa and have worked for an accredited employer for more than 2 years.

NZ.name: Talent (Arts, Culture, Sports) Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for New Zealand residency if you have a Talent (Arts, Culture, Sports) Work Visa and have been actively involved in New Zealand in your field for more than 2 years.

NZ.name: Trafficking Victim Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you are in New Zealand and already have a trafficking victim work, student or visitor visa.

NZ.name: Transport Work to Residence Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this resident visa if you currently have a job or job offer with an accredited employer, and have worked in New Zealand for 24 months in an approved transport job.

NZ.name: Victims of Family Violence Resident Visa
NZ.purpose: You can apply for this visa if you have experienced family violence and have been in a partnership with a New Zealand citizen or resident. It allows you to live and work in New Zealand permanently.

NZ.name: Work to Residence Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa if you currently have a job or job offer with an accredited employer, and have worked in New Zealand for 24 months in a Green List Tier 2 job that meets our requirements.

NZ.name: Interim Visa
NZ.purpose: This visa is normally given automatically to allow you to stay in New Zealand if your visa expires while we are assessing your application for another temporary visa.

NZ.name: Limited Visa
NZ.purpose: Apply for this visa to visit New Zealand temporarily for an express purpose. Once you have achieved your purpose, you must leave New Zealand or apply for another Limited Visa.

NZ.name: Refugee Claimant Visitor Visa
NZ.purpose: If you are in New Zealand and have applied for refugee or protection status, this visa lets you stay here while we process your refugee or protected person claim.

SCHENGEN.name: Visa-free short stay
SCHENGEN.purpose: Short stays for nationalities that do not need a Schengen visa (e.g. Serbia, the US, the UK).
SCHENGEN.note: At most 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries. Entries and exits are recorded by the Entry/Exit System (EES).

SCHENGEN.name: ETIAS travel authorisation
SCHENGEN.purpose: Online authorisation that visa-free travellers will need before a short stay.
SCHENGEN.note: Not in operation yet — the EU says it starts in the last quarter of 2026. Not a visa; the 90/180 rule still applies.

SCHENGEN.name: Uniform Schengen visa (type C)
SCHENGEN.purpose: Short stays for tourism, business, family visits or events in the Schengen area.
SCHENGEN.maxValidity: Up to 5 years (multiple entry, issued step by step)
SCHENGEN.note: Never more than 90 days in any 180-day period, whatever the visa validity says.

SCHENGEN.name: Visa with limited territorial validity (LTV)
SCHENGEN.purpose: Exceptional short-stay visa valid only for the Schengen country (or countries) named on it.
SCHENGEN.note: Valid only in the countries printed on the visa sticker.

SCHENGEN.name: Airport transit visa (type A)
SCHENGEN.purpose: Changing planes in the international zone of a Schengen airport — for nationalities that need it.
SCHENGEN.note: Does not allow entry into the Schengen area.

SCHENGEN.name: National long-stay visa (type D)
SCHENGEN.purpose: Stays over 90 days in one Schengen country (study, work, family), issued by that country under its own rules.
SCHENGEN.note: Also allows up to 90 days in any 180 in the other Schengen countries while valid. Rules differ per issuing country.

SCHENGEN.name: Residence permit of a Schengen country
SCHENGEN.purpose: Living in a Schengen country (work, study, family, long-term residence, EU Blue Card).
SCHENGEN.note: No day count in the issuing country; up to 90 days in any 180 in the other Schengen countries.

TR.name: Visa exemption
TR.purpose: Tourism or business visits for nationalities exempt from a visa (e.g. Serbia, most of Europe).
TR.note: At most 90 days in any 180 days — binding for every foreigner, whatever the visa says. Passport valid 60 days beyond your allowed stay.

TR.name: e-Visa
TR.purpose: Online visa for tourism or business for eligible nationalities, from the official site evisa.gov.tr only.
TR.maxValidity: Usually 180 days, single or multiple entry, for stays of 30 or 90 days
TR.note: Only for tourism or commerce. At most 90 days in any 180 days — binding for every foreigner, whatever the visa says. Passport valid 60 days beyond your allowed stay.

TR.name: Sticker visa — tourism or business
TR.purpose: Tourism, business meetings, conferences, fairs, for those who cannot get an e-Visa.
TR.note: Consulates issue at most 90 days of stay. At most 90 days in any 180 days — binding for every foreigner, whatever the visa says. Passport valid 60 days beyond your allowed stay.

TR.name: Transit visa
TR.purpose: Passing through Türkiye to another country (airport or land transit).

TR.name: Work visa
TR.purpose: Entry to take up a job; a work permit from the Ministry of Labour must be issued.
TR.maxValidity: Up to 90 days, then a work permit
TR.note: Apply for the work permit within the first days after arrival.

TR.name: Study visa
TR.purpose: Entry to study at a Turkish school or university; followed by a student residence permit.
TR.maxValidity: Up to 90 days, then a student residence permit

TR.name: Other purpose visas
TR.purpose: Journalism, archaeological excavation, documentary filming, official duty, crew, sporting and cultural events.

TR.name: Work permit
TR.purpose: Working in Türkiye for an employer, or as an independent professional; also counts as a residence permit.
TR.maxValidity: Up to 1 year first, then up to 2 and 3 years; indefinite after 8 years

TR.name: Turquoise Card
TR.purpose: Highly qualified workers, investors, scientists, artists and athletes; leads to indefinite permission.

TR.name: Short-term residence permit
TR.purpose: Staying longer than 90 days for research, owning a home, business ties, training, exchange programmes, tourism, medical treatment and more.
TR.maxValidity: Up to 2 years at a time, renewable
TR.note: No day count while the permit is valid.

TR.name: Family residence permit
TR.purpose: Spouse, children and dependent children of a Turkish citizen or of a foreigner with a residence permit.
TR.maxValidity: Up to 3 years at a time

TR.name: Student residence permit
TR.purpose: Students in associate, bachelor, master or doctoral programmes at Turkish universities.
TR.maxValidity: Length of the studies, renewed yearly

TR.name: Long-term residence permit
TR.purpose: After at least 8 years of continuous legal residence in Türkiye.

TR.name: Humanitarian residence permit
TR.purpose: Granted in special cases, e.g. the best interest of a child, or when someone cannot be removed.
TR.maxValidity: Up to 1 year at a time

TR.name: Residence permit for victims of human trafficking
TR.purpose: Victims of human trafficking, to recover and decide whether to cooperate with the authorities.

US.name: ESTA — Visa Waiver Program
US.purpose: Visit for tourism, business or transit without a visa — only for Visa Waiver Program nationalities.
US.maxValidity: 2 years (or until the passport expires)
US.note: Not a visa. At most 90 days per visit, no extension and no change of status.

US.name: B-1/B-2 Visitor visa
US.purpose: Tourism, visiting family, medical treatment (B-2) or business meetings, conferences, negotiations (B-1).
US.maxValidity: Up to 10 years — depends on your nationality
US.note: The visa only lets you travel to the border. CBP sets how long you may stay on your I-94, usually 6 months (by law up to 1 year). Your I-94 date is what counts.

US.name: C-1 / C-1/D Transit visa
US.purpose: Passing through the United States to another country, or joining a ship or aircraft as crew.
US.maxValidity: Depends on your nationality
US.note: Transit admissions are limited to 29 days by law (8 CFR 214.2(c)).

US.name: D Crewmember visa
US.purpose: Crew on a ship or aircraft arriving in the United States.
US.maxValidity: Depends on your nationality
US.note: Crew shore leave (landing permit) is limited to 29 days.

US.name: F-1 / F-2 Academic student
US.purpose: Full-time study at a university, college, high school or language school; F-2 for spouse and children.
US.maxValidity: Depends on your nationality; the stay lasts as long as your studies (D/S)
US.note: Admitted for "duration of status" — as long as you study as shown on your I-20, plus 60 days.

US.name: M-1 / M-2 Vocational student
US.purpose: Vocational or other non-academic study (e.g. technical schools, flight schools).
US.maxValidity: Up to 1 year at a time
US.note: Admitted for the length of the program, at most 1 year at a time, plus 30 days.

US.name: J-1 / J-2 Exchange visitor
US.purpose: Exchange programs: research scholars, interns, au pairs, summer work-travel, teachers, physicians; J-2 for family.
US.maxValidity: Depends on your nationality; the stay lasts as long as your program (D/S)
US.note: Admitted for the program dates on your DS-2019, plus 30 days. Some J-1s must spend 2 years at home afterwards.

US.name: H-1B / H-4 Specialty occupation
US.purpose: Work requiring a university degree, sponsored by a US employer; H-4 for spouse and children.
US.maxValidity: Up to 3 years, extendable to 6 years
US.note: The stay is set by the approved petition (I-797) and your I-94, not by a day count.

US.name: H-1B1 Specialty occupation (Chile, Singapore)
US.purpose: Degree-level work for citizens of Chile or Singapore.
US.maxValidity: Up to 18 months, renewable

US.name: H-2A Temporary agricultural worker
US.purpose: Seasonal or temporary farm work for a US employer.
US.maxValidity: Up to 1 year, at most 3 years in total

US.name: H-2B Temporary non-agricultural worker
US.purpose: Seasonal or peak-load work outside agriculture (hotels, construction, landscaping…).
US.maxValidity: Up to 1 year, at most 3 years in total

US.name: H-3 Trainee or special education visitor
US.purpose: Training not available at home (not graduate medical training), or special-education exchange.
US.maxValidity: Up to 2 years (18 months for special education)

US.name: L-1 / L-2 Intracompany transferee
US.purpose: Managers, executives (L-1A) or specialists (L-1B) moving to a US office of the same company; L-2 for family.
US.maxValidity: L-1A up to 7 years, L-1B up to 5 years in total

US.name: O-1 / O-2 / O-3 Extraordinary ability
US.purpose: Extraordinary ability or achievement in science, arts, education, business, athletics, film or TV; O-2 support staff, O-3 family.
US.maxValidity: Up to 3 years, extendable 1 year at a time

US.name: P-1 Athlete or entertainment group
US.purpose: Internationally recognised athletes, teams and entertainment groups (P-1A / P-1B).
US.maxValidity: Up to 5 years for athletes; for the event for groups

US.name: P-2 / P-3 / P-4 Artists and entertainers
US.purpose: Performers in a reciprocal exchange (P-2) or a culturally unique program (P-3); P-4 for family.
US.maxValidity: Up to 1 year

US.name: Q-1 International cultural exchange
US.purpose: Sharing your country's culture through a work-and-training program (e.g. theme parks).
US.maxValidity: Up to 15 months

US.name: R-1 / R-2 Religious worker
US.purpose: Ministers and religious workers of a recognised religious organisation; R-2 for family.
US.maxValidity: Up to 30 months, at most 5 years in total

US.name: E-1 / E-2 Treaty trader or investor
US.purpose: Substantial trade with, or investment in, the United States by citizens of treaty countries; family included.
US.maxValidity: Depends on your nationality; each admission up to 2 years, renewable
US.note: Only for nationalities with a US treaty of commerce.

US.name: E-3 Specialty occupation (Australia)
US.purpose: Degree-level work for Australian citizens; family included.
US.maxValidity: Up to 2 years, renewable

US.name: TN / TD USMCA professional
US.purpose: Professionals from Canada or Mexico in listed occupations; TD for family.
US.maxValidity: Up to 3 years, renewable

US.name: I Foreign media representative
US.purpose: Journalists, film crews and other foreign media working in the United States.
US.maxValidity: For the length of the assignment

US.name: CW-1 / E-2C Northern Mariana Islands
US.purpose: Transitional workers (CW-1) and investors (E-2C) for the Northern Mariana Islands only.
US.maxValidity: Up to 1–3 years

US.name: K-1 / K-2 Fiancé(e) visa
US.purpose: Fiancé(e) of a US citizen travelling to marry in the United States; K-2 for their children.
US.maxValidity: Up to 6 months, single entry
US.note: You must marry within 90 days of entry, then apply for a green card; the stay cannot be extended.

US.name: K-3 / K-4 / V Family awaiting a green card
US.purpose: Spouse or children of a US citizen (K-3/K-4) or of a permanent resident (V) waiting for an immigrant visa.
US.maxValidity: Up to 2 years

US.name: A-1 / A-2 / A-3 Diplomats and government officials
US.purpose: Diplomats and foreign government officials on official duty, their family and staff.
US.maxValidity: For the length of the posting

US.name: G-1 to G-5 International organisations
US.purpose: Staff of international organisations (e.g. UN, World Bank, IMF), their family and staff.
US.maxValidity: For the length of the assignment

US.name: NATO-1 to NATO-7
US.purpose: Representatives and staff of NATO and their family.
US.maxValidity: For the length of the assignment

US.name: T / U Victims of trafficking or crime
US.purpose: Victims of human trafficking (T) or of certain crimes (U) who help law enforcement; family included.
US.maxValidity: Up to 4 years

US.name: S Witness or informant
US.purpose: People providing critical information about a criminal or terrorist organisation, requested by US law enforcement.
US.maxValidity: Up to 3 years

US.name: Immigrant visa / Green card
US.purpose: Living permanently in the United States — through family, employment, the Diversity Visa lottery or other categories.
US.maxValidity: Permanent residence (card renewed every 10 years)
US.note: No day count: you live in the United States. Long absences abroad can put the green card at risk.
